'''Zbigniew Ciesielski''' (<small>Polish pronunciation</small>: {{IPAc-pl|'|z|b|i|g|ń|e|f|-|ć|e|'|ś|e|l|s|k|J|i}}; 1 October 1934 – 5 October 2020<ref>Obituary https://www.impan.pl/wydarzenia/aktualnosci/2020/nekrolog-zbigniew-ciesielski.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20201008073256/https://www.impan.pl/wydarzenia/aktualnosci/2020/nekrolog-zbigniew-ciesielski.pdf |date=2020-10-08 }}</ref>) was a Polish mathematician specializing in [[functional analysis]] and [[probability theory]]. He served as the President of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] from 1981 to 1983.

== Education and career ==
Ciesielski was born in [[Gdynia]], [[Poland]]. He received in 1960 his doctorate from the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan]] with dissertation ''{{lang | pl | O rozwinięciach ortogonalnych prawie wszystkich funkcji w przestrzeni Wienera}}'' (On orthogonal developments of almost all functions in Wiener space) under the supervision of [[Władysław Orlicz]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy | id = 51936 | name = Zbigniew Ciesielski}}</ref>

He has been a professor at the Mathematical Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences since 1969 and a member of the Academy since 1973. In 1974 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Vancouver.<ref>{{cite book|author=Ciesielski, Z.|chapter=Bases and approximations by splines|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vancouver, B.C., 1974|volume=2|year=1975|pages=47–52|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Congress|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/200673979}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Ciesielski, Z.|year=1983|chapter=Spline bases in spaces of analytic functions|title=''In:'' Canadian Math. Soc. Conference Proceedings|volume=3|pages=81–111|isbn=9780821860045|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fdN_BpsVrxwC&pg=PA81}}</ref> He was President of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] from 1981 to 1983.

Ciesielski's main areas of research are [[functional analysis]], in particular [[Banach space#Schauder bases|Schauder base]]s in [[Banach space]]s, and [[probability theory]], in particular the [[Wiener process|mathematical theory of Brownian motion]].

==Awards and decorations==

* 1964: {{ill|Stefan Banach Prize|de|Stefan-Banach-Preis}}
* 1974: [[Order of Polonia Restituta]]: Knight's Cross 
* 1984: [[Order of Polonia Restituta]]: Officer's Cross 
* 1992: {{ill|Stefan Banach Medal|de|Stefan-Banach-Medaille}}
* 1988: {{ill|Polish State Award|pl|Odznaka Nagrody Państwowej}} of 1st degree
* 2004: Honorary Member of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]]
* 2014: [[Honorary degree]] of the [[University of Gdańsk]]
